items.followUp: What is meant by heat transfer?

rubric.why: Checks that heat is identified as transferred energy.
rubric.description: States that heat is energy transferred.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying heat as transferred energy.

rubric.why: Checks the condition that causes the transfer of heat.
rubric.description: States that heat transfer occurs because of a temperature difference.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the temperature-difference cause.

modelAnswer: Heat is energy transferred from one body to another because of a difference in temperature.

items.followUp: Convert 320 K into temperature on the Celsius scale.

rubric.why: Checks the Kelvin-to-Celsius conversion relation.
rubric.description: Writes the relation for converting kelvin to Celsius.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct conversion relation.

rubric.why: Checks the converted temperature and its unit.
rubric.description: Calculates the temperature as 27 °C.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct answer with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: T = 300 K
Formula: T(°C) = T(K) − 273
Substitution: T = 300 − 273
Answer: T = 27 °C

items.followUp: Derive the second equation of motion using a velocity-time graph.

rubric.why: Checks that displacement is obtained from the area under the velocity-time graph.
rubric.description: Identifies the area as that of a trapezium and writes the displacement relation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the trapezium area and its displacement expression.

rubric.why: Checks the acceleration relation used to express time.
rubric.description: Uses the acceleration equation and rearranges it for time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either equivalent relation.

rubric.why: Checks the substitution of the expression for time into the displacement relation.
rubric.description: Substitutes the acceleration-based expression for time into the displacement equation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct substituted expression.

rubric.why: Checks the correctly derived third equation of motion.
rubric.description: Rearranges the substituted expression to obtain the third equation of motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either equivalent final equation.

modelAnswer: Draw a velocity-time graph with time on the horizontal axis, velocity on the vertical axis, and a straight line from velocity u at time 0 to velocity v at time t.
The displacement s is the area under the velocity-time graph, which is a trapezium.
Area of trapezium: s = 1/2 (u + v)t
Acceleration: a = (v − u)/t, so t = (v − u)/a
Substitute for t: s = 1/2 (u + v)(v − u)/a
Multiply by 2a: 2as = (u + v)(v − u)
Use the difference of squares: 2as = v² − u²
Therefore, v² = u² + 2as

items.followUp: Define kinetic energy and derive its formula.

rubric.why: Checks the definition of potential energy.
rubric.description: Defines potential energy as energy possessed due to position.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that potential energy is due to a body's position.

rubric.why: Checks that the lifting force is identified as the body's weight.
rubric.description: States that the force required to lift the body equals its weight, mg.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the force as mg.

rubric.why: Checks the work calculation for lifting the body through height h.
rubric.description: Calculates the work done against gravity as mgh.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct work calculation.

rubric.why: Checks the resulting potential-energy formula.
rubric.description: States the formula for gravitational potential energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for P.E. = mgh.

modelAnswer: Potential energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its position.
When a body of mass m is lifted through a height h, the force applied equals its weight, F = mg.
Work done = force × displacement = mg × h = mgh.
This work is stored as potential energy; therefore, P.E. = mgh.

items.followUp: A force of 60 N acts on an area of 2 cm². Calculate the pressure in pascals.

rubric.why: Checks the given force and the conversion of area to SI units.
rubric.description: States the force and converts the contact area to square metres.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct force and area conversion.

rubric.why: Checks the pressure formula.
rubric.description: Writes pressure as force divided by area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

rubric.why: Checks substitution of the given values in SI units.
rubric.description: Substitutes the force and converted area into the pressure formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct substitution with units.

rubric.why: Checks the numerical calculation.
rubric.description: Calculates the pressure as 5 × 10⁵.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct numerical result.

rubric.why: Checks that the final pressure is stated with its SI unit.
rubric.description: Gives the final pressure in pascals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct final answer with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: Force, F = 75 N
Given: Contact area, A = 1.5 cm² = 1.5 × 10⁻⁴ m²
Formula: Pressure, P = F/A
Substitution: P = 75 N/(1.5 × 10⁻⁴ m²)
Answer: P = 5 × 10⁵ Pa

items.followUp: Differentiate between a base quantity and a derived quantity, giving one example of each.

rubric.why: Checks the defining property of base units.
rubric.description: States that base units are independent and are not derived from other units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this distinction.

rubric.why: Checks how derived units are formed.
rubric.description: States that derived units are formed by combining base units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this distinction.

modelAnswer: Base units are independent units that are not derived from other units; for example, the metre (m).
Derived units are obtained by combining base units; for example, the metre per second (m/s).

items.followUp: What is the least count of a measuring tape marked in millimetres?

rubric.why: Checks the definition of least count.
rubric.description: Defines least count as the smallest measurement an instrument can measure accurately.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition.

rubric.why: Checks the least count of a metre rule.
rubric.description: Gives the least count of a metre rule.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either equivalent value.

modelAnswer: The least count of an instrument is the smallest measurement that it can measure accurately.
The least count of a metre rule is 1 mm (0.1 cm).
